mainTopic: Injuries that make an animal a טריפה: a cut חוט השדרה (in animals and birds), a missing liver, and a pierced lung
overview: This amud covers three kinds of injury that can make an animal a טריפה. First it asks whether שמואל's rule that a cut in the חוט השדרה is a טריפה 'until' the first פרשה includes that spot or stops before it. רב פפא and רבי ירמיה each build a follow-up question on one side of that doubt. A proof from a ברייתא is turned aside: the ברייתא is about the third branch only. Next, רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש disagree about how far down a bird's spinal cord counts, and עולא tells a story about בן פזי that might support ריש לקיש. The גמרא then turns to a missing liver. רב יוסף settles two משניות that seem to clash by assigning them to רבי חייא and רבי שמעון ברבי. רב פפא rules that a כזית must remain both near the gallbladder and where the liver is attached, and questions about the shape of that כזית end in תיקו. Last, the גמרא starts on a lung with a hole: it asks which of the lung's two layers counts, and says a hole in the outer layer alone is not a problem.

steps.title: Does 'until' include the first branch area or not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל's word 'until' (עד) includes the first פרשה area itself or stops before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does 'until' mean 'until and including,' or perhaps 'until and not including'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking what שמואל meant by 'until' the first פרשה. Does a cut right in that area make the animal a טריפה, or not?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל gave a border: a cut in the חוט השדרה is a טריפה down to the first פרשה. The question is whether the border area itself is inside the rule ('including') or outside it ('not including'). This doubt is the base for the next two questions.

keyTerms.meaning: Until, but not including the endpoint
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even after proper שחיטה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. The word 'until' comes from שמואל's earlier rule about the חוט השדרה, which the גמרא is still discussing.

phrases.english: Does 'until' mean until and including,
phrases.notes: This is about שמואל's earlier rule: a cut in the spinal cord is a טריפה 'until' the first branch of nerves.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא עַד וְלֹא עַד בַּכְּלָל?
phrases.english: or perhaps until and not including?

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד וְעַד בַּכְּלָל, אוֹ דִּלְמָא עַד וְלֹא עַד בַּכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the meaning of שמואל's border word 'until' from the earlier discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the area of the first פרשה is included in the zone where a cut makes the animal a טריפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: Every follow-up question in this section depends on which way this doubt goes.

steps.title: רב פפא asks about the opening of the branch
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks: if 'until' does not include the first פרשה, what is the law for a cut exactly at the opening of the branch?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: If you say 'until and not including,' what is the law for a cut at the mouth of the branch?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא takes one side of the doubt, 'not including,' and asks a sharper question built on it. What about a cut exactly at the spot where the branch begins?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first פרשה area is outside the clear rule, we need to know exactly where that area starts. The 'mouth' of the branch is right on the edge, so it is unclear whether it counts as part of the branch area or as the part above it.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks a question he cannot settle (a dilemma)
If you conclude that (building a question on one possible answer)
The mouth (opening) of the branch, where it splits off

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
If you say,
'until and not including,'
what is the law of the mouth of the branch?
phrases.notes: He means a cut exactly where the nerves start to branch off from the cord.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a follow-up question on the 'not including' side of step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a cut at the very opening of the first פרשה counts as inside the branch area or above it.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה asks about the branch itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks: if 'until' does include the first פרשה area, what is the law if the branch itself is cut?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: If you say 'until and including,' what is the law of the branch itself?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה takes the other side of the doubt, 'including,' and asks his own follow-up. What if the branch nerves themselves are cut, not the main cord?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a cut in the cord at the first פרשה area makes the animal a טריפה, maybe the branch nerves count as part of the חוט השדרה too. Or maybe they are separate, and cutting them does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: The branch itself (the pair of nerves that splits off)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
If you say,
'until and including,'
what is the law of the branch itself?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 2, but builds on the opposite ('including') side of step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether cutting the branch nerves of the first פרשה makes the animal a טריפה like the cord itself.

steps.title: Attempted proof: the branch is treated like flesh
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying a cut פרשה is judged like ordinary flesh, and suggests this includes even the first and second branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The branch is judged like flesh. Doesn't this mean even the first and second branch?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רבי ירמיה's question from a ברייתא. The ברייתא says a branch is treated like flesh, so cutting it would not make the animal a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'the branch' means any branch, including the first one, then רבי ירמיה is answered: cutting the first branch is not a טריפה. The proof depends on reading the ברייתא as talking about every branch.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that... (suggesting a reading to prove a point)
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The branch shall be judged like flesh.
phrases.notes: Like flesh means it is not treated as the spinal cord, so cutting it does not make the animal a טריפה.

phrases.english: Isn't it referring to the first and second branch?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to resolve רבי ירמיה's question from step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That cutting the first פרשה itself does not make the animal a טריפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: 'הפרשה תידון כבשר,' read as covering even the first and second branches.

steps.title: Rejection: the teaching means only the third branch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the ברייתא is talking only about the third branch, not the first or second.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means the third branch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The ברייתא's 'branch' is the third one, so it tells us nothing about the first branch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By limiting the ברייתא to the third branch, the גמרא leaves open that the first and second branches may still count like the cord. So רבי ירמיה's question stays unanswered.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא 'the branch is like flesh' is read as the third branch only, so the law of cutting the first branch itself stays an open question.

phrases.english: No, the third.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide רבי ירמיה's question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the ברייתא covers all branches, but it can be read as the third branch alone.

steps.title: Where the spinal cord ends in a bird
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי says a bird's spinal cord extends to below the wings. ריש לקיש says it extends only to between the wings.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a bird: רבי ינאי says the spinal cord reaches below the wings. ריש לקיש says it reaches until between the wings.
steps.whatsHappening: After discussing an animal's spinal cord, the גמרא now asks the same question about a bird. Two אמוראים disagree about how far down the important part goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cut in the spinal cord above its lower limit makes the bird a טריפה. רבי ינאי puts the limit lower, below the wings, so more of the cord counts. ריש לקיש puts it higher, between the wings, so a cut below that point does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: The wings (where the wings join the body)
Up to the point between the wings

steps.confusionAlert: The disagreement is about the bottom limit of the חוט השדרה: how far down a cut in the cord still makes the bird a טריפה.

phrases.english: With a bird,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יַנַּאי אוֹמֵר: לְמַטָּה מִן הָאֲגַפַּיִם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai says: below the wings,

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: עַד בֵּין אֲגַפַּיִם.
phrases.english: and Reish Lakish said: until between the wings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the animal's spinal cord to the parallel question in a bird.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ינאי: the critical zone reaches below the wings. ריש לקיש: only until between the wings.

steps.title: עולא's story about בן פזי checking a bird
steps.stepSummary: עולא saw בן פזי check a bird only as far as between the wings before he left for the נשיא. עולא does not know whether he stopped because that was the limit or out of respect for the נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: I was standing before בן פזי. They brought him a bird, and he checked it until between the wings. Then the נשיא's house sent for him, and he got up and left. I don't know if he stopped because there was no need to check further, or because of the honor of the נשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא tells a story that seems to support ריש לקיש. Then he admits the story might not prove anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בן פזי stopped on purpose at the point between the wings, that would show he holds like ריש לקיש. But he may have stopped only because the נשיא called him, which would leave the question open. So the story raises a possible proof and leaves it undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: The honor owed to the נשיא, the head of the Jewish community

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עוּלָּא: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּבֶן פַּזִּי,
phrases.english: Ulla said: I was standing before ben Pazi,
phrases.notes: This is רבי שמעון בן פזי.

phrases.english: and they brought a bird before him,
and he checked until between the wings,
and the house of the Nasi sent for him,
and he got up and went,
and I do not know

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא צְרִיךְ לְמִבְדַּק טְפֵי,
phrases.english: whether it was because one does not need to check further,
or because of the honor of the Nasi.

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רבי ינאי and ריש לקיש stays open. עולא's story could support ריש לקיש, but it is not a clear proof.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּבֶן פַּזִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that might decide the argument in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The view of ריש לקיש that the limit is between the wings
steps.raayaSupportSource: What בן פזי did in practice, as עולא saw it
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: עולא himself admits that בן פזי may have stopped only out of respect for the נשיא.

steps.title: Two משניות disagree about leftover liver
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה suggests that any leftover piece of liver keeps the animal kosher. A later משנה requires a כזית to remain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'If the liver was removed' (and nothing was left, it is a טריפה). So if anything at all was left, it is kosher, even if it is less than a כזית. But we learned in another משנה: If the liver was removed and a כזית of it remained, it is kosher. That suggests less than a כזית is not enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה, the missing liver. It points out a contradiction with a later משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה makes an animal טריפה only when nothing of the liver is left. That implies even a tiny piece is enough. The later משנה specifically says a כזית, which implies that less than a כזית makes it טריפה. The two inferences clash.

phrases.english: The liver was removed, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה, which says that if the liver is gone, the animal is a טריפה.

phrases.english: So if anything of it remained, it is kosher,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא הָוֵי כְּזַיִת,
phrases.english: even though it is not an olive-bulk,
But didn't we learn:

phrases.aramaic: נִיטַּל הַכָּבֵד וְנִשְׁתַּיֵּיר הֵימֶנָּה כְּזַיִת – כְּשֵׁרָה!
phrases.english: If the liver was removed and an olive-bulk of it remained, it is kosher!
phrases.notes: This is a later משנה in this פרק (on 54a).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic from the משנה, unrelated to the bird discussion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied ruling of our משנה that any leftover piece of liver is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A later משנה requires a כזית, which implies that less than a כזית is not enough.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the two משניות follow different sages
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that one משנה follows רבי חייא and the other follows רבי שמעון ברבי. He proves this with a story where each of them acted differently with a small leftover piece of liver.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is not difficult. One משנה follows רבי חייא, and the other follows רבי שמעון the son of רבי. As in this story: רבי חייא threw it away, and רבי שמעון the son of רבי dipped it and ate it. Your memory aid: 'The rich are stingy.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the contradiction from step 8 by saying the two משניות follow two different sages who disagreed in a real case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once there was an animal with less than a כזית of liver left. רבי חייא threw it away, because he holds it is a טריפה, like the later משנה. רבי שמעון ברבי dipped it in sauce and ate it, because he holds any leftover is enough, like our משנה. The memory aid helps you remember that the rich רבי שמעון ברבי did not let the meat go to waste.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult, there is no contradiction
Threw it away (treated it as a טריפה)
Dipped it in sauce (to eat it, treating it as kosher)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Stingy' here is not a criticism. It means the rich person was careful not to waste food, so he took the lenient view and ate it.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is not difficult,

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא, הָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי,
phrases.english: this is Rabbi Ḥiyya, that is Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi,
phrases.notes: Each משנה follows a different sage: the כזית משנה goes with רבי חייא, and ours goes with רבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא זָרֵיק לַהּ,
phrases.english: like that case where Rabbi Ḥiyya threw it away,
phrases.notes: The case was a liver with less than a כזית left.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי מְטַבֵּיל לַהּ,
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi dipped it,
and your mnemonic: "The rich are stingy."
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון, the son of the wealthy נשיא, did not let the meat go to waste.

steps.whatToRemember: The two משניות do not contradict each other. Each follows a different sage. רבי חייא says less than a כזית of liver is a טריפה, and רבי שמעון ברבי says any leftover keeps the animal kosher.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns each משנה to a different sage (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to reflect one view, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each משנה follows a different sage: רבי חייא requires a כזית, and רבי שמעון ברבי accepts any amount.

steps.title: רבי זירא tells the fleeing sages where the olive-bulk must be
steps.stepSummary: While running from an army, רבה and רב יוסף meet רבי זירא. He tells them the required כזית of liver must be at the spot of the gallbladder.
steps.simpleTranslation: An army came to פומבדיתא, and רבה and רב יוסף ran away. רבי זירא met them and said: 'Refugees! The כזית the חכמים spoke about must be in the area of the gallbladder.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story, and inside it רבי זירא gives a ruling about exactly where the leftover כזית of liver has to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The later משנה quoted in step 8 requires a כזית of liver to remain for the animal to be kosher. Now רבי זירא adds a new detail: not just any כזית counts. It has to be the part near the gallbladder.

phrases.english: A certain army that came to Pumbedita,
Rabbah and Rav Yosef fled.
Rabbi Zeira met them.
He said to them: Refugees!
The olive-bulk that they spoke of must be in the place of the gallbladder.
phrases.notes: This is the כזית of liver that must be left so the animal stays kosher, from step 8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines where the required כזית of liver must be located.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The required כזית of liver must be at the spot of the gallbladder.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: the olive-bulk must be where the liver is attached
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה gives a different location: the place where the liver 'lives,' meaning where it is attached.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה says: the כזית must be in the place where the liver 'lives.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer to the same question: where must the כזית of liver be?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא said the gallbladder area. רב אדא בר אהבה points to a different spot, the place where the liver hangs attached to the body. Now we have two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where it lives, meaning where the liver is attached

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava says:
In the place where it lives.
phrases.notes: He means the spot where the liver is attached to the other organs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing location for the כזית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The required כזית of liver must be at the place where the liver is attached.

steps.title: רב פפא: we need an olive-bulk in both places
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that both opinions must be satisfied. A כזית must remain at the gallbladder and also at the attachment spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore, we need a כזית at the gallbladder, and we also need a כזית where the liver is attached.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the practical ruling after the two opinions: to be safe, we follow both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we don't decide between רבי זירא and רב אדא בר אהבה, we need both requirements. If either spot is missing a כזית, the animal is not kosher.
steps.whatToRemember: For the animal to stay kosher, a כזית of liver must remain both near the gallbladder and where the liver is attached.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Therefore,
we require an olive-bulk in the place of the gallbladder,
and we require an olive-bulk in the place where it lives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the two opinions into one stricter practical rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A כזית is required in both locations.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה asks about a leftover in pieces or in a strip
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks whether the כזית counts if it is made of small pieces, or if it is shaped like a long thin strip.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: If the כזית is made of small pieces that add up, what is the law? If it is like a strip, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה asks a question about the shape of the leftover liver. The גמרא is setting up a list of questions that will stay unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know the amount needed is a כזית. Now the question is whether the amount alone is enough, or whether it must be one solid, olive-shaped piece.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a strip, long and thin

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
If it is gathered together, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Small bits of liver that only add up to a כזית when counted together.

phrases.english: If it is like a strip, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for more detail about the כזית just required.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a כזית count if it is in scattered pieces or shaped like a strip?

steps.title: רב אשי asks about a flattened olive-bulk, and the questions stay open
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether a flat, spread-out כזית counts. The גמרא ends all these questions with תיקו: they remain unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: If the כזית is spread flat, what is the law? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds one more shape question, and then the גמרא says none of these questions get an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A flat piece may have the right amount but not be thick like an olive. The word תיקו closes רבי ירמיה's questions and רב אשי's question together. None of them is decided.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the animal is kosher. It means the גמרא never decided the question.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
An olive-bulk spread flat, what is the law?
Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third shape question, then closes all of them unresolved.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a flat, thin כזית count?
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All the shape questions remain unresolved (תיקו).

steps.title: רבי זריקא asks about a liver hanging only by its membranes
steps.stepSummary: רבי זריקא asks רבי אמי what the law is if the liver came loose and stays attached only by its membranes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זריקא asked רבי אמי: If the liver became detached and is held only by its membranes, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question: the liver is whole, but it has come loose from its normal attachments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the cases were about how much liver is left. Here nothing is missing. The liver is only loosened, so the question is whether that alone makes the animal a טריפה.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זְרִיקָא מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zerika asked Rabbi Ami:
If the liver became detached
and is attached by its membranes, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זְרִיקָא מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a missing liver to a loosened but whole liver.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a liver that hangs only by its membranes a problem?

steps.title: רבי אמי: the detachment does not matter, both opinions are satisfied
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says he doesn't see why this detachment should matter. The whole liver is there, so both the gallbladder spot and the attachment spot are present.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I don't know what this detachment matters. According to the one who says the gallbladder area, it is there. According to the one who says the attachment area, it is there too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers that the animal is fine, using the two opinions from steps 10 and 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only thing that matters is that a כזית remains in the right place. Since the whole liver is still there, both spots have their כזית. Being loosened alone changes nothing.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּלְדּוּל זֶה אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מַהוּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: This detachment, I do not know what it is.
phrases.notes: He means: I don't see why this loosening should matter at all.

phrases.english: If according to the one who says in the place of the gallbladder,
that is here.

phrases.aramaic: אִי לְמַאן דְּאָמַר בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁהִיא חַיָּה –
phrases.english: If according to the one who says in the place where it lives,
that is here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּלְדּוּל זֶה אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מַהוּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The loosened liver is fine, because the needed כזית is present according to both opinions.

steps.title: A lung with a hole: which layer is meant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the next case in the משנה, a lung with a hole. רב, שמואל and רב אסי identify which of the lung's two layers is meant, and there are two versions of what they said.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A lung that was perforated': רב, שמואל and רב אסי say this means the upper layer. Some say they said the lower layer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה. It reports a statement about which lung layer the משנה is talking about, in two versions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lung has two layers, an outer one and an inner one. One version says the three אמוראים meant the outer layer. Another version says they meant the inner layer, so the גמרא needs a way to remember which is right.

phrases.english: The lung that was perforated,
Rav and Shmuel and Rav Asi, who say:
The upper membrane.
And some say: the lower membrane.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, the perforated lung.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's perforated lung refers to one specific layer. It is debated whether that is the outer or the inner layer.

steps.title: רב נחמן's memory sign: the red robe the lung rests in
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives a memory sign: 'the rose-colored robe in which the lung rests.' This points to the red, inner layer as the one meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן: Your sign is the rose-colored robe in which the lung rests.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a memory sign to settle which of the two versions to remember.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner layer of the lung is red and wraps the lung like a robe. So the sign tells us to remember the version that says the inner layer.
steps.whatToRemember: The perforated lung in the משנה refers to the red inner layer, remembered by the sign of the red robe the lung rests in.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said that Rav Nachman said:
And your sign is the rose-colored robe
in which the lung rests.
phrases.notes: The inner layer is red and wraps the lung, so this sign points to the inner layer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסִימָנָיךְ כִּיתּוּנָא דְּוַרְדָּא דְּמַנְּחָא בֵּיהּ רֵיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles which of the two versions in step 17 to remember.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The relevant layer is the red inner membrane.

steps.title: If only the outer layer is pierced, the inner layer protects
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says it is obvious that a hole in the outer layer alone does not make the animal טריפה, because the whole inner layer protects the lung. It supports this with a statement of רבה, which begins here and continues past this line.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if the outer layer was pierced and the inner layer was not, the inner layer protects the lung. This fits what רבה said, for רבה said: a lung whose outer skin was peeled off...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes what we just learned, that the inner layer is the one that counts, and draws one clear result from it. Then it starts quoting רבה as backing, and his statement continues in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When just the outer layer is pierced and the inner layer is whole, the inner layer acts as a shield and the animal is kosher. The גמרא calls this obvious because of רבה's case of a lung that lost its outer skin, which shows the inner layer can protect the lung by itself. Calling this case obvious sets up the harder reverse case, an inner hole with the outer layer whole, which the גמרא takes up on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. The גמרא says this case needs no proof.
Was peeled, its skin came off

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the layers. The outer layer (עִילָּאָה) being pierced is not a problem here. What happens if only the inner layer (תַּתָּאָה) is pierced is not settled here. The גמרא takes that up on the next amud.

phrases.english: It is obvious: if the outer layer was pierced
and the inner layer was not pierced,
the inner layer protects the lung,
in line with Rabba, as Rabba said:
this lung that was peeled

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא: אִי אִינְּקִיב עִילָּאָה וְלָא אִינְּקִיב תַּתָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the perforated-lung topic from steps 17-18. It states the obvious case, supported by רבה, as a setup for the reverse case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If only the outer layer of the lung is pierced and the inner layer is whole, the inner layer protects the lung and the animal is not טריפה.
